Here n=20

X: number of children to be cured

X=0,1,2,3\ldots 20

p=0.90,\ q=0.1

$p(x)=\left\{\begin{matrix}{}^{20}_{x}C(0.90)^x(0.10)^{20-x}, & x=0,1,2,3,\ldots,20\\ 0, & \textit{otherwise}\end{matrix}\right.$

(i) P(all 20 will be cured) =P(X=20)={}^{20}_{20}C(0.90)^{20}(0.10)^{20-20}=0.12158

(ii) P(exactly 18 will be cured) =P(X=18)={}^{20}_{18}C(0.90)^{18}(0.10)^{20-18}=0.28518

(iii) P(at least one will be cured) =1-P(no one will be cured)

=1-P(X=0)

=1-{}^{20}_{0}C(0.90)^0(0.10)^{20-0}

=1-0 (approximately)

$=1$

Example 3.10

In Peshawar 42 % of the population has type-A blood. Consider, taking a sample of size 4. Let Y denotes the number of persons in the sample with type-A blood. Find (i) P(Y=0) (ii) P(Y=1) (iii) P(0\le Y\le 2) and (iv) P(0<Y\le 2)

Solution:

Given that p=0.42, q=0.58, n=4

Y: number of persons in the sample with type-A blood

Y=0,1,2,3,4

\therefore p(y)=\left\{\begin{matrix}{}^{4}_{y}C(0.42)^y(0.58)^{4-y}, & y=0,1,2,3,4\\ 0, & \textit{otherwise}\end{matrix}\right.

(i)\quad P(Y=0)={}^{4}_{0}C(0.42)^0(0.58)^{4-0}=0.11316

(ii)\quad P(Y=1)={}^{4}_{1}C(0.42)^1(0.58)^{4-1}=0.32779

(iii)\quad P(0\le Y\le 2)=P(Y=0)+P(Y=1)+P(Y=2)

=0.11316+0.32779+{}^{4}_{2}C(0.42)^2(0.58)^{4-2}

=0.44095+0.35609

=0.79700

(iv)\quad P(0<Y\le 2)=P(Y=1)+P(Y=2)

=0.32779+0.35605=0.68384

Example 3.11

A machine produces 10 per cent defective items. Ten items are selected at random. Find the probability of not more than two items being defective.

Solution:

\text{We have } p=10\%=\frac{10}{100}=\frac{1}{10}

\therefore q=\frac{9}{10}

n=10

X: number of defective items

$X=0,1,2,3\ldots 10$
